speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's office. I understand you are presenting with chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To begin our evaluation, how many times per day are you having bowel movements, and what specific characteristics do you notice in the stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like classic "tennessee" symptoms—urgency, mucus, and a feeling of incomplete evacuation. Given the camping history and the outbreak among your group, are you experiencing any blood in your stool or fever? REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_and_Sensitivity, Stool_Ova_and_Parasites.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Campylobacter jejuni infection (likely post-camp outbreak gastroenteritis progressing to reactive enteritis/colitis).
